facts.fact: The guide recommends that a one-person service business usually be on camera, and that a business with a team feature 2-3 specific named employees in its creative rotation.
facts.quote: If you're a one-person business, you should usually be on camera. If you have a team, feature 2-3 specific employees by name in your creative rotation.

facts.fact: The guide recommends showing a 5-7 second sequence of footage from real work in a service business spot.
facts.quote: A 5-7 second sequence of footage from real work

facts.fact: The guide recommends that one trust signal be used per service business spot, delivered cleanly, because multiple trust signals dilute each other.
facts.quote: One trust signal per spot, delivered cleanly. Multiple trust signals dilute each other.

facts.fact: The guide gives 'Over 8,000 jobs completed in the East Bay' as an example of a volume trust signal for a service business spot.
facts.quote: Over 8,000 jobs completed in the East Bay.

facts.fact: The guide gives '5-star average from 1,200+ reviews' as an example of a quality trust signal for a service business spot.
facts.quote: 5-star average from 1,200+ reviews.

facts.fact: The guide gives 'Serving Phoenix homeowners for 23 years' as an example of a local-tenure trust signal for a service business spot.
facts.quote: Serving Phoenix homeowners for 23 years.

facts.fact: The guide states that in a product business spot the product should be in frame for at least 20 seconds, using kitchen goods as the example.
facts.quote: the kitchen goods are in the frame for at least 20 seconds

facts.fact: The guide says sensory micro-moments in product spots are often 1-2 seconds long.
facts.quote: often 1-2 seconds, but they're the moments viewers remember

facts.fact: The guide gives a tension-and-resolution example in which a roughly 5-second setup is followed by a resolution playing out across the next 20 seconds of a product spot.
facts.quote: That's a 5-second setup; the resolution can play out across the next 20.

facts.fact: The guide states that 30 seconds is the right length for both service and product TV spots, which are calibrated for 30-second delivery on streaming inventory.
facts.quote: Both formats are calibrated for 30-second delivery on streaming inventory.

facts.fact: The guide gives 'order this weekend, free shipping over $50' as an example of a specific product spot call to action.
facts.quote: order this weekend, free shipping over $50

facts.fact: The guide gives '20% off your first order with code TV20' as an example of a direct product spot call to action.
facts.quote: 20% off your first order with code TV20

facts.fact: Adwave says its platform can generate a 30-second TV-ready creative from a business's website in roughly 2 minutes, with no per-spot cost beyond the platform subscription.
facts.quote: Platforms like Adwave can generate 30-second TV-ready creative from a business's website in roughly 2 minutes, at no per-spot cost beyond the platform subscription.

facts.fact: The page states that a custom 30-second TV spot from a production agency typically cost $3,000-$15,000 (a general industry figure, not an Adwave number).
facts.quote: A custom 30-second spot from a production agency typically cost $3,000-$15,000

facts.fact: The page says AI-generated creative variations are each produced in 2-5 minutes, in contrast to a quarterly $5,000 production cycle.
facts.quote: all produced in 2-5 minutes each rather than a quarterly $5,000 production cycle

facts.fact: The page recommends refreshing TV creative for both service and product businesses every 60-90 days.
facts.quote: plan to refresh creative every 60-90 days

facts.fact: The page recommends a 4-6 week rotation of CTV creative variations to produce enough signal to identify the stronger creative.
facts.quote: a 4-6 week rotation usually produces enough signal to identify the stronger creative

facts.fact: The page says CTV platforms typically allow running two or three creative variations in rotation.
facts.quote: Most CTV platforms allow you to run two or three creative variations in rotation

facts.fact: The page advises that a product should be in the frame for at least 20 of the 30 seconds of a product TV spot.
facts.quote: The product needs to be in the frame for at least 20 of the 30 seconds

facts.fact: The page advises that both service and product TV spots use their final 3-5 seconds to lock in the brand name, URL, and visual identity.
facts.quote: Both formats need the final 3-5 seconds to lock in your brand name, URL, and visual identity.

facts.fact: In the service business template, the first 5 seconds are a hook acknowledging the moment of need, and the final 5 seconds (0:27-0:30) carry a soft CTA plus brand lock-in.
facts.quote: **0:27-0:30:** Soft CTA + brand lock-in.

facts.fact: In the product business template, the final 3 seconds before the close (0:27-0:30) are reserved for a direct CTA and brand lock-in.
facts.quote: **0:27-0:30:** Direct CTA + brand lock-in.

facts.fact: In the service business template, 5-7 seconds of actual footage from real jobs is shown between 0:15 and 0:22.
facts.quote: 5-7 seconds of actual footage from real jobs.

facts.fact: The page states that in 2025 TV-quality 30-second creative mostly required a professional production crew, and that by 2026 this is increasingly no longer necessary.
facts.quote: In 2025, mostly yes. In 2026, increasingly no.

facts.fact: The page says the 'Brand lock-in' and 'one message per spot' guidance applies to both formats, and the page specifically says the trust-plus-offer combination in 30 seconds dilutes both.
facts.quote: Trying to be both a trust-builder AND a direct-response offer in 30 seconds dilutes both.

facts.fact: Per the vendor, service-business TV spots build trust through real people, acknowledged discomfort, and one clean trust signal.
facts.quote: Service spots build trust through real people, acknowledged discomfort, and one clean trust signal.

facts.fact: Per the vendor, product-business TV spots build desire through product-as-hero framing, moments of use, and specific direct CTAs.
facts.quote: Product spots build desire through product-as-hero framing, moments of use, and specific direct CTAs.

facts.fact: Per the vendor, hybrid businesses should run multiple TV spots rather than trying to combine service and product approaches into one spot.
facts.quote: Hybrid businesses run multiple spots rather than trying to combine the two.
